question: You shoot one photo for the product page — but can your buyer turn it around?

hook_visual.intent: flat product photos the buyer can only see from one angle, cut into a spinnable object

points.claim: idol turns a single picture of an object into a full three-D Gaussian splat, including the sides the picture never showed, in about two seconds.
points.spoken: Drop one photo into idol — you pull out a full three-D model you can turn with your mouse. Even the sides your camera never saw are drawn in. In about two seconds.
points.source_note: Model card: 'Idol turns one picture of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat… including the sides the picture never showed' + 'can run in under 2 seconds'.

visual.intent: photo beside its live 3D, cursor drags it around

points.title: PHOTO IN, 3D OUT

points.claim: The pipeline removes the background, frames the object, and writes a standard 3DGS .ply that opens in Blender — no studio or turntable.
points.spoken: No studio, no turntable. It cuts the background, frames the object, and hands you a file that opens in Blender — so you drag it straight onto the product page or into a game.
points.source_note: Model card: 'it removes the background, frames the object and generates up to 1,048,576 Gaussians, written as a standard 3DGS .ply' — .ply opens in any Gaussian-splat viewer (Blender reads .ply).

visual.intent: background stripped off the same object, .ply into a Blender window

points.title: STRAIGHT INTO BLENDER

points.claim: It runs on your own consumer GPU — 7.2 GB VRAM — with no cloud call or waitlist.
points.spoken: Your own graphics card runs it — about seven gigabytes. No cloud call, no waitlist.
points.source_note: Model card: 'It runs on consumer GPUs, using 7.2 GB of VRAM and can run in under 2 seconds.' Cloud-free reading: it's a local SDK run.

visual.intent: gauge on your card, no cloud chips

points.title: YOUR GPU, NOT THE CLOUD

points.claim: Try it free in the browser demo, or run one command on your own machine.
points.spoken: Or type one command on your own machine — python idol sample, photo.jpg — and your first model is done.
points.source_note: Model card demo badge -> huggingface.co/spaces/speridlabs/idol; SDK: pip install -e . + python -m idol.sample --image photo.jpg --mode real.

visual.intent: the free demo door, then the command typing itself

points.title: ONE COMMAND

points.claim: On the lab's own benchmark it edges TripoSplat and TRELLIS on every visual column, and it was the number-one trending model on Hugging Face today.
points.spoken: On the lab's own tests it beat both big image-to-three-D tools on every visual score — and it topped the trending list today.
points.source_note: Benchmark table: Idol bold in SSIM, LPIPS, IoU, DINOv2, CLIP, sharpness distance vs TripoSplat/TRELLIS. HF trending #1, score ~765 on 2026-11-08.

visual.intent: bars with idol on top, trending badge

points.title: PROOF ON ITS OWN TESTS

catch: One boundary: it makes single objects — your sneaker, your mug, your product — not whole rooms. Everything your photo shows, you still get.

steps: you keep every angle you shot

cover.visual: a plain product photo on the left, the same object as a spun Gaussian splat on the right

Full-bleed paper with a giant '2s' chip, a VRAM bar at 7.2 GB, and a small violet splat orbiting in the corner.

cta: So skip the reshoot. Comment IDOL and I'll pin the link.
